recipes.name: Renee's Strawberry Rhubarb Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.1 ounce) package pastry for a double crust
1 tablespoon turbinado sugar (such as Sugar in the Raw®)

steps.text: Whisk cornstarch and 1 tablespoon water together in a large bowl until combined; stir in rhubarb, strawberries, white sugar, vanilla extract, cinnamon, and lemon juice. Set filling aside for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Roll out half dough on a floured surface to fit a 9-inch pie plate; place in pie plate and refrigerate until ready to use. Roll top crust on a floured surface into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 1-inch wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel; set aside.

Stir filling; pour into the prepared pie plate. Moisten the rim of the crust with a small amount of water. Start with the longest dough strips and lay the first 2 in an X in the center of the pie. Alternate horizontal and vertical strips, weaving them in an over-and-under pattern. Use the shortest strips for the edges of the lattice. Press strips down on crust rim to seal; trim excess. Beat egg white and 1 teaspoon water together in a small bowl; brush over lattice top. Sprinkle with turbinado sugar. Wrap aluminum foil strips around edges of pie.

Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C); bake until crust is golden and filling is bubbling, 40 to 45 more minutes. Remove aluminum foil for the last 10 minutes of baking time. Cool pie completely before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Renee's Strawberry Rhubarb Pie
raw_recipe.description: Renee's strawberry rhubarb pie recipe is made without tapioca — just strawberries, rhubarb, and cinnamon with a lattice crust for a winning combo.

review.reviewBody: Strawberry Rhubarb Pie is my absolute favorite, but I've never made it until now. My pie turned out excellent, with the perfect consistency and combination of tart and sweet. I reduced the sugar to 1 cup and added 3 tablespoons of quick tapioca to the filling. I wanted to make sure it wasn't runny as well as keep a lot of the tartness from the rhubarb. I don't like to add a lot of sugar to fruit pies because of the natural sweetness of the fruit. Overall, it was delicious!

Turned out a lot better than I expected! Everyone enjoyed it! Made a double recipe (risky for a first trial!) with locally grown strawberries (slightly thawed from frozen and sliced) and rhubarb from my garden. I did add the cinnamon and vanilla, but also added 1.5 Tbsp flour per recipe to the fruit mixture. I used commercial pie shells that I half baked and lined with toasted bread crumbs before filling with the fruit mixture. I opted to just top the pie with a crisp topping. Otherwise, I followed the recipe’s directions. The pie tasted fruity and light, not too sweet or runny. I think the cinnamon and vanilla gave depth to the flavour of this pie. I would definitely make this again, and it’s a tasty way to use up my rhubarb!

I had lost my relied upon recipe so I searched for something similar. Renee's recipe is OK, but I did not want to make pastry, so I used a good commercial one. Instead of topping the pie with pastry dough, I used Phyllo dough. I keep this in my freezer to use on pies. I cut two 2 inch chunk of phyllo, unfolded it and spreaded the fluffy "flakes" over the top. Phyllo is delicate, light and not so fattening. I also added 2 Tbs, not 1, of water to the corn starch mixture. I used only 2/3 C of sugar, and 2 tsp of lime juice. Withheld cinnamon because it tends to overpower the fruit taste and gives the pie a muddy color. I dotted the pie mixture with 4 Tbs. of butter before spreading the Phyllo dough. I put it in the oven and covered the pie top lightly with a piece of aluminum foil. I removed the foil, 8 minutes before the pie was finished. Delicious! My name also is Renee.

I doubled the recipe. I was short 1 cup of rhubarb and substituted some fresh black cherries (I pitted) that I had. I cut back the sugar to 2 cups instead of 2 1/2 cups. I tripled the cornstarch/water mixture and I still had trouble with some soupiness (which I drained real quick before putting in pies.). This had very good flavor and the black cherries didn’t interfere with this great tasting pie. Oops, almost forgot— I added 1/4 tsp. of nutmeg. BTW, make sure you put a piece of parchment paper between your pie and the cookie sheet you place it on in the oven. It’ll save you some clean-up, my dears.

Love how the flavor turned out! I decided to use up all the strawberry and rhubarb I had, so it ended up being about 4 cups each of fruit. It fits because it cooks down, but I knew the juice would overflow (which it did) so I placed the pie on a baking sheet to contain juice. I adjusted the other ingredients accordingly. Lastly, for those wondering like me, do you really need the foil on the outside crust? If you want an even color, then yes. Although I don't mind, because my crust, while dark, still tasted good.

I increased the cornstarch from 2 to 3 tbsp and added 2 tbsp of flour, as well as 1/4 tsp of nutmeg. I also doubled the water and vanilla and reduced the sugar to 1 cup. I think it was still too sweet, next time I'll use 1/2 cup of sugar. I used a 10 in glass pan instead of the recommended 9 in and didn't have any spillover while baking. I let it sit for about 6 hours to cool completely before cutting and it kept its shape.

Other than adding a 1/4 cup of maple syrup and after letting the mixure sit for 30 minutes I strain the juice into a pot. Boil the juice until thickened. Let cool for about 15 minutes. Add back to the rhubarb strawberries before placing into the pie shells. Makes a less juicy pie. We love this recipe. My wife and I just made 11 pies for friends and family.
I added 3 tbls corn starch and used a solid top crust that had small vents cut in it. It turned out delicious and not watery. I used 1 1/4 cups sugar and no sugar on top crust.

Just as I suspected, 2 Tablespoons is not enough thickening agent. It was a strawberry rhubarb soup, not pie. I'd follow this recipe again but probably use more like 1/4-1/3 cup corn starch. I think as long as it is dissolved in some liquid beforehand it will dissolve fine and the taste will be gone. I would have cooked it longer to let it thicken up and let the liquid evaporate out a bit, but the crust was getting such a burned look on it I decided soup for dessert it is!

This pie turned out delicious, but I was very nervous that I would make yet another soupy rhubarb pie after reading the reviews. I decided to try a few of the other reviewers' suggestions. I increased the corn starch to 1/4 cup, sprinkled tapioca on the bottom crust plus substituted a little less than 1/4 cup of strawberry jello for 1/4 cup of the sugar. It may have been overkill, but I can't stand runny, soggy rhubarb pie! Next time, I will probably eliminate the egg white wash because the crust turned brown too quickly.

BEST PIE EVER!
As others suggested I used 1C sugar. I used 3T corn starch and mixed it in with the sugar mixture. Omitting the water.
I’ve got a lot of rhubarb & strawberries in my freezer! Can’t wait to make this again!

Homemade crust. Ruth’s Grandmas pie crust. Substitute butter for shortening. Makes a lot but freezes well.
First time making strawberry Rhubarb pie, never had it before. I made it for my husband and it's now a Big hit at our house. Easy to make.
I like iusing cornstarch rather than flour. The whole pie was sweet and tart. Easy to make.
It was an easy recipe to follow, I didn’t add or subtract any ingredients and my family raved over this pie. Thanks for the recipe!!

I love this recipe because the ingredients are simple and instructions are straightforward. I didn't want to have to go buy tapioca starch, or figure out how many lbs of rhubarb I cut up. (Like in other recipes) the pie is delicious, it's not super thick like you would expect a apple pie to be, because it's a berry pie. Its supposed to be a little runny lol. Anyway the only "Tweak" I do is I always pre bake my bottom crust. Just prick the crust and put it in the oven for like 5-8 minutes, before adding the fruit filling. Thank you for a delicious recipe.
Loved it. I added an additional teaspoon of cornstarch and it was still pretty runny.
I didn’t quite have enough rhubarb, so I added more strawberries. It was absolutely fabulous!
Excellent Recipe. Second time making it. Did have to add a bit more cornstarch after the fruit sat for 30 minutes, but it turned out great and was super yummy. Will make again.

My family loved this recipe, and I will use it again! It was gone in less than a day. My one complaint is that it was a bit runny, even though I upped the cornstarch. Maybe use about a 1/4 cup when you make this, with a tablespoon or so more of water.
Excellent. Like another commenter suggested, I strained and reduced the liquid in the mixture and then put it back in. My pie did not come out soupy!
